comparison: Both address antibiotic resistance findings (C33-C37, C119). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with caveat about phenotypic confirmation and sampling bias. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, describing genomic analyses as 'high quality' without raising specific concerns about resistance findings.

Perfect overlap on virulence gene analysis (C38-C54, C117-C118). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED but notes gene presence doesn't confirm expression. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, explicitly stating 'without knowing their frequency in the broader E. coli population it is hard to know the significance' - a more critical stance on interpretability.

Both address statistical comparison of virulence factors (C55). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with caveat about biological significance. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, noting 'genomic analyses are high quality' without specific critique of this finding. Agreement on data quality.

Perfect overlap on serotyping data (C56-C67). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes ELISA validation strengthens claims. Peer reviewers describe 'genomic analyses are high quality' without raising concerns. Strong agreement.

Perfect overlap on recrudescence case documentation (C68-C79, C107). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes small sample size limitation. Peer reviewers state 'case study investigations are convincing' and note the study 'documents bacterial persistence and reinfection.' Strong agreement on evidence quality.

Both address treatment failure concerns related to resistance (C102-C103). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting lack of clinical outcome data and that no patients experienced resistance-related treatment failure. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, accepting clinical relevance for 'people involved in management of neonatal meningitis patients.' Disagreement on certainty level.

High overlap on dysbiosis characterization (C89-C92). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for dysbiosis documentation but notes inability to prove causation without pre-treatment samples. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED as part of 'convincing' case studies. Agreement on data quality.

High overlap on study limitations (C110-C113). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes authors 'appropriately acknowledge significant limitations.' Peer reviewers accept these as factors affecting scope without disputing them. Strong agreement on limitation acknowledgment.

Both address virulence feature interpretation (C29-C30, with peer also including C104). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting causal claims require experimental validation and alternative explanations not excluded. Peer reviewers also rate UNCERTAIN, stating 'without knowing their frequency in the broader E. coli population it is hard to know the significance.' Strong agreement on uncertainty.

High overlap on gut reservoir detection (C80-C88, with peer also including C93-C94, C114-C116). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for detection methods but rates gut reservoir hypothesis separately as UNCERTAIN (R10). Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, stating findings are 'convincing' and 'of clinical importance.' Disagreement on certainty of reservoir hypothesis implications.

Substantial overlap on phylogenetic and sequence typing methodology (C22-C28). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with caveats about geographic/temporal bias. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, describing 'population genomic analyses are comprehensive.' Agreement on data quality.

Both address K1 capsule virulence speculation (C104). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting this is 'explicitly presented as speculation' and conflates correlation with causation. Peer reviewers also rate UNCERTAIN, noting interpretation is speculative. Strong agreement on speculative nature.

Partial overlap on gut reservoir hypothesis (C94, C114-C116). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting Patient 3 had undetectable E. coli yet still had recrudescence, and therapeutic implications are premature. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, stating 'This finding is of clinical importance as it suggests that decolonisation of the gut could be helpful.' Significant disagreement on certainty and clinical implications.

Partial overlap on complete genome sequences (C31-C32, C120). OpenEval rates collection establishment as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers explicitly identify complete genomes as a strength, stating they 'will serve as useful references for future studies.' Agreement on value.

Both address collection establishment and geographic representation (C20-C21, C109). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED but acknowledges geographic limitations. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, explicitly noting 'it is not clear how well the results reflect the global diversity of NMEC' and challenging generalizability. Disagreement on overall assessment - OpenEval more accepting despite noting same limitation.
